posturePlanQualifier: one schema read grounds it, nothing else reaches the database
posturePlanTitle: Plan mode drafts, and never runs what it drafted
postureUnsupportedQualifier: plan mode drafts here, and the operations workflow still runs
postureUnresolvedQualifier: no connection is resolved, so no engine has been established
postureUnresolvedTitle: Agent mode has no connection to execute on
postureWidenedHeadline: Reads only, and one statement in your editor
postureWidenedTitle: Reads only, and one statement lands in your editor
postureReadsTitle: Agent mode reads, under a boundary the engine enforces
handoverTerms: The run always produces its answer on its own read-only path, bounded to {rows} rows and {seconds} seconds. Tick this and it will also put that statement in your editor and run it there — on the connection the run was opened on, at the editor's {editorRows}-row limit and with no time limit. It is the same database-enforced read-only session either way, so writes and DDL are refused by the engine rather than by reading the statement. Statements whose plan reads as expensive, or which the run measured as slow, are put in the editor without being run.
posturePlanBody: Plan mode never executes the statement it wrote, on any engine — production included. Its one reach is the schema capture that grounds it: metadata only, no data rows, and it is where the inventory in Run details came from. On {engines} that capture is itself a catalog read; on every other engine it asks the provider to describe its own schema.
postureUnsupportedTitle: Agent mode has no read-only statement path on {engine}
postureUnsupportedBody: Agent mode executes only where the provider implements a database-native read-only statement path — {engines}. On {engine} a run whose workflow sends a statement is refused when it is started, before a run is opened. The operations workflow still runs here, because it sends no statement at all: it calls the curated reporting methods every provider implements. Plan mode drafts on every engine.
postureUnresolvedBody: Agent mode executes only where the provider implements a database-native read-only statement path — {engines}. No connection is resolved here, so this panel cannot say which engine you are on, or whether it is one of those: until one is resolved, agent mode executes nothing. The operations workflow sends no statement at all, so it runs wherever a connection does, and plan mode drafts on every engine.
postureWidenedQualifier: {rows} rows, no time limit, same read-only session
postureReadsQualifier: {rows} rows and {seconds} s per statement, enforced by the engine
postureReadsBody: Agent mode runs statements it wrote itself, in a read-only session the database enforces, bounded to {rows} rows and {seconds} seconds each. Writes and DDL are refused by the engine rather than by reading the statement. Nothing reaches your editor unless you tick the hand-over when the run opens.
sqliteCost: On SQLite a read is not interrupted when it runs long: it blocks other writers and this application until it finishes.

consentFrozen: This is decided by the request that opens the run and stays what it was: a later request cannot widen a run the server already holds.
guardChecked: Checked as a bounded read against the captured inventory. Nothing was executed.
guardCheckedNoInventory: Checked as a bounded read. Nothing was executed.
guardUnexamined: Not examined: the statement guard reads SQL, and this engine's statements are not SQL.
guardObjection: The statement guard did not read this as a bounded read ({reason}).
applyGuardUnread: The statement guard reads SQL and this engine's statements are not SQL, so nothing examined this draft.
applyNamesUnread: The name check reads SQL too, so the names it uses were not looked for in anything.
applyNamesUnchecked: Nothing checked the names it uses.
applyGuardObjection: The statement guard did not read this as a bounded read ({reason}), so nothing here establishes that running it would only read.
applyUnknownNames: It names {count} {noun}(s) the inventory this run read does not hold, so it may not run as written.
guardUnreadNote: The statement guard reads SQL, and this engine's statements are not SQL — so nothing examined this draft. It is drafted, not run — nothing has happened to your data — but nothing here has established anything about it, for or against.
namesUnreadNote: The names in this statement were not checked: the check that would do it reads SQL, and this engine's statements are not SQL.
noInventoryNote: No schema inventory was read for this run, so the names in this statement were not checked against anything.
unknownNamesNote: These names are not in the inventory this run read, so the statement may not run as written:
executionCaveat: The run executed nothing. What was checked is what this run read of the schema, which records what exists rather than what your role is permitted to read.
refusalNote: This run drafted no statement. What it says is missing, and what it needs from you, are in its own words below.
spendFloorNote: What is counted comes from the run's ledger, which records less than the server charges, so a spend shown here is a floor, never a ceiling.
unclassifiedFailure: This run ended as failed and its own record names no reason for it. The server log is where the cause is.
guardObjectionNote: {objection} It is drafted, not run — nothing has happened to your data — but nothing here establishes that running it would only read.
spendFloorTitle: Figures are a floor, not the spend
evidenceCount: Evidence · {count, plural, one {# citation} other {# citations}}
recordedElapsed: {seconds} s since this run's first recorded entry
failureModelUnavailable: The model provider is not configured or could not be reached.
failureRateLimited: The model provider is limiting this key's requests. Waiting a minute usually clears it.
failureUnauthorized: The model provider rejected the configured credentials.
failureEngineUnsupported: The agent cannot run on this database engine: it offers no read-only execution profile.
failureCredential: This connection's agent credential cannot be used: check that both the agent user and password are set, that the password still decrypts under the current secret key, and that no connection string is set beside it.
failureConnection: This run's database connection no longer resolves on the server.
failureInternal: The server could not carry this run. The reason is in the server log.
planEstimateCaveat: Estimates only: these plans were described, not executed. EXPLAIN ANALYZE is policy-denied because it would run the statement.
notAppliedCaveat: Not applied: nothing here runs this statement.
handoverNone: Nothing was sent to the editor; applying the statement is the user's own action.
handoverApplied: The statement is in your editor and was not run there.
handoverExecuted: This run handed the statement to your editor to run: it ran on your connection, under the editor's own limits, and what it did with it is visible there rather than here.
pointInTimeCaveat: A moment, not a history: this reading says what the engine reported as it was taken.
accessMixed: a mix of index and full scan
accessUnknown: an access path this reading could not interpret
stopNoReport: The model stopped without composing a cited report.
stopDeadline: The run reached its time limit before it finished.
stopModelTimeout: The model did not answer in time. Starting the run again is reasonable.
stopTurnLimit: The run reached its step limit before it finished. What it had gathered is above.
stopPlanComplete: The model finished its plan and stopped. Planning mode has no tools, so it composed no report.
stopArrivedLate: A stop was requested before this ending: the run took no further database step, and finished what it already had in hand.
shortfallNoReport: The run finished without composing a cited report, so nothing it found was written down.
shortfallEmpty: Every result the report cited came back empty, so the answer rests on nothing.
shortfallNoPlan: The run produced no plan at all.
shortfallNoStatement: The run described how it would approach the question and never wrote the statement, and it did not say what was missing either.
shortfallNoComparison: No before-and-after plan comparison was recorded, and no index was recommended: a query optimization rests on one or the other.
shortfallNoEvidence: The index was recommended without citing a plan this run read, so nothing the engine said backs it.
shortfallNoProfile: No table was profiled, so the state of the data was never established.
shortfallNoReading: The report rests only on the schema inventory this run read, and on no reading of what the engine is doing, so nothing it says was measured on this server.
shortfallNoAnswer: The run reported what it found but never produced an answer to show, so there is nothing to put in front of you.
shortfallUncited: The run presented one result as the answer and its report rests on other evidence entirely, so the claims and the picture are not about the same thing.
shortfallCancelled: The run was stopped before it could finish.
readingUnsupported: This engine serves no reading of that kind
readingOverBudget: The reading was larger than the run may carry
citationUnresolved: not in the part of this run's timeline the rail has read
timelineGuardUnread: The statement guard reads SQL, and this engine's statements are not SQL, so nothing here examined this draft at all. Nothing about it was established, for or against.
timelineGuardChecked: The statement guard read this as a bounded read and had no objection, which is not a promise about what it does.
timelineNamesUnread: The name check reads SQL too, so the objects this draft names were not looked for in anything.
timelineNoInventory: No schema inventory was read for this run, so the names it used were not checked at all.
draftUnexamined: Statement drafted — not examined by the statement guard
draftNotRead: Statement drafted — not classified as a read
stopCheckpoint: the run takes no further database step; work already in hand, such as a report, still finishes
guidanceLastTurn: Told this is its last turn
guidanceRead: Asked to read the database itself
guidancePresent: Asked to present the result first
guidanceCite: Asked to cite what it read
guidanceCompare: Asked to compare the plans it holds
timelineGuardObjection: The statement guard did not read this as a bounded read ({reason}). It is marked, not blocked: running it is your decision.
namesAllFound: Every {noun} it names is in the inventory this run read — which records what exists, not what your role is permitted to read.
namesNotFound: {count} name(s) it uses are not in the inventory this run read, so it may not run as written.

refusalTryPlan: Plan mode needs no tools, so it may still work with this model: it reasons about your question and drafts a statement for you to run yourself. It runs no statement of yours and writes nothing. Try it, or configure a different model — one that passes the probe — for a run that investigates the database itself.
refusalNoStream: This endpoint answered without streaming, and plan mode reads the same stream, so it would produce nothing here either. A different model, or an endpoint that streams, is what gets an answer.
refusalDifferentModel: A different model, one that passes the probe, is what gets a run that reads the database.
threadConnectionChanged: Connection changed, so this question started a new conversation.
threadDisabled: Conversation context is switched off on this server, so every question starts on its own.
threadRepointed: This connection was re-pointed after the earlier step ran, so this question started a new conversation. Follow-ups from here continue on the connection as it points now.
threadUnavailable: The earlier step could not be carried into this question, so it started on its own.
objectiveSummary: The objective this run was opened with:
modelCannotDrive: This model cannot drive an agent run.
timelineEmpty: No activity yet. A run's steps appear here as they are recorded.
classifying: Reading your objective to choose a workflow.
freshConversation: Your next question will start a new conversation.
editObjective: Edit the objective and ask again
replaceObjective: Replace the objective with the suggested one
reserveInfo: What is kept back for the report
changeWorkflowName: Stop this run and open a new {workflow} run
setupCount: Run setup · {count, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}}
interruptedThread: The conversation this browser was in ({count, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}}, {id}) ended when the page reloaded. Your next question starts a new one.
threadSteps: Conversation: {count, plural, one {# step} other {# steps}} before this one
automaticNote: Automatic reads your objective on the server and opens the run for the workflow it names. Naming one yourself skips that reading entirely.
planSummaryLocation: The statement, what the name check found and what applying it would and would not establish are in the answer at the top of this rail.
changeWorkflowNote: Changing it stops this run and opens a new one. Stopping is observed between turns, so it is not instant: the run ends at its next checkpoint. The new run gets a new id, and this one stays in the ledger with everything it recorded.
replacementFailed: This run was not stopped, so nothing new was opened: it is still going and still spending its budget. The line above is what the server answered. Ask again, or use Stop and start a new run once it has ended.
budgetCaveats: Every ceiling is per drive, so a run resumed after a restart starts each of them again and these totals can read past a single drive's ceiling. What is counted comes from the run's ledger, which records less than the server charges: the schema capture's catalog reads are not itemized, and a completed read reports the engine's own elapsed time rather than the span the budget was charged. So a spend shown here is a floor, never a ceiling.
sqliteTimeout: On SQLite a statement over its timeout is refused once it returns, not interrupted while it runs.
budgetUnknown: Every ceiling here is per workflow, and Automatic decides the workflow from your objective when the run opens — so the figures are stated once the run has one, and by the run's own record.
resultRetention: A run's stored rows are released when the run ends, so a result can be shown only while its run is still going.
handoverDeclined: It was not run: this run was opened on {connection} and your editor has moved to a different one since. The answer would have arrived in a tab that is connected somewhere else, so nothing was executed. The statement is below — take it yourself if you want it on the connection you are on now.
seedConfigUnreadable: The server could not read its own connection configuration, so it cannot resolve a connection for a run. This is not a problem with {connection} — the server log says what failed.
connectionBrowserOnly: {connection} cannot be rebuilt on the server: its settings live in this browser. A run re-resolves its connection there after a restart, so it can only investigate a connection the server holds too.
missingDuration: The ledger holds no duration for {count} of this run's charged statements, so that spend is not in the figure above.
budgetLimits: Each statement gets {seconds} s, each drive {minutes} min and at most {turns} model turns.
reserveNote: The last {turns} model turns and the last {seconds} s are kept back for the report: whichever it reaches first, the run is asked once to stop and report what it has established. So a run that ends short of these figures was asked to stop rather than having given up, and its claims still cite what it read. A plan run is never asked, having no report to compose.
engineRefusalConsequence: No run was opened. The notice above says why, and what still runs on this engine.
openedClassified: Opened as {label}, read from your objective.
openedUnclassified: Opened as {label}: your objective could not be classified, so the run investigates rather than being told what it is for.
openedUnrecorded: Opened as {label}. Nobody here chose it, and this run's record does not say whether your objective was read into it or fallen back from.

startError: The run could not be started ({status})
stopError: The run could not be stopped ({status})
